summary: Seek bounded message pages through body-free temporal selectors

replay.detail: Opening an older database backfills local message selector headers from current message projections and retained canonical claims in short, resumable chunks before readers are served. Starting a backfill invalidates existing page cuts. No authoritative claim replay or body-copy inventory is introduced; ordinary pages fold only selected message bodies.

schema.detail: Adds local_client_message_selectors_v1: a body-free header/pending/quarantine table with twenty-two indexes and seven source-change triggers, completed-cut and resumable backfill/fold markers. Five retained-cut eligibility indexes contain retired headers only; historical open pages combine bounded live and retired index branches, avoiding duplicate historical-index writes on ordinary sends. The seventh trigger queues full folds/quarantine for message repairs and repaired replacement reselections. local_client_message_fold_batches stores only batch IDs/legacy wire-position prefix counts and skips scratch persistence for single-row completed prefixes. local_client_message_publications stores retention cohorts only when a retirement needs its first covering publication, plus the initial bootstrap cohort; cut advances without retirement add no cohort. Retired headers remain until their first covering publication is older than the cursor lifetime; bounded cohort cleanup always preserves the latest stored cohort. The fold marker retains canonical keys and selection scalars, never content or attachments. Suspended full folds retain append progress/extend their cut; destructive epoch changes or newly dirty metadata-only bases restart them. Maintenance uses at most 64 claim/prefix rows and 16 subjects per transaction with a cooperative 10 ms work budget; all cleanup is bounded. A weakly owned daemon worker drains remaining work through independent writer loans; idle checks do not borrow/commit the writer, and last-task completion wakes readers/events. Malformed desired JSON skips the subject's header, warns and increments a local counter. In final two-order 128-send/128-close real-append bursts, send WAL was 125,789 bytes per commit without selectors and 189,101.8125 with them (+50.33%); close WAL was 112,366.8125 and 226,374.9375 bytes per commit respectively. Enabled WAL fell 14.18% for sends and 4.25% for closes relative to the pre-optimization enabled run; additional close WAL per 128-commit burst fell from 15,878,480 to 14,593,040 bytes. Send p50 was 1.957/1.889 ms with selectors versus 1.226/1.321 ms without. Send p95 deltas were +2.766/+46.165 ms; close p95 deltas were +48.462/+45.052 ms. These observed tails are unexplained; no timing improvement or contention attribution is established. Earlier page-read measurements predate final changes and need remeasurement. Cursor epochs also fence repaired replacement reselections; earlier body-version tables/triggers are removed idempotently. Registry and replication compatibility digests, authoritative claims and claim formats are unchanged.

rules.detail: Canonical claim-log checkpoint rules, the schema registry digest and shared projection digests are unchanged. SQLite WAL checkpoint scheduling during startup backfill changes as described under downtime; it is distinct from canonical checkpoints. Deletion or repair that destroys a retained message cut, or a selector backfill start, invalidates that traversal instead of returning a partial successful page.

compatibility.detail: Message JSON, recipient/actor filters, ordering, reminder selection and snapshot-consistent traversal are preserved. Pending selector tasks are invisible; ordinary incomplete maintenance serves and pins the last fully published frontier. Desired-projection deletion immediately clears declaration-derived fields and eligibility, expires existing cursors and appears on fresh pages before reconciliation completes; retained intent.desired claims do not restore deleted fields. Destructive claim update/delete, message repair and repaired replacement reselection expire old cursors and insert one durable born_index=-2 quarantine marker per subject; fresh pages temporarily omit that subject until replacement reconciles and its cut is published. The desired-projection shortcut requires an indexed subject/kind check proving no declaration after the requested cut. Continuations bind exact store cut, snapshot, filters, limit, position and expiry. Tampered, expired, evicted, restarted or deletion-invalidated cursors return HTTP 410/page-cursor-expired. Delivery presence remains live on each page while delivery age retains the first request time.

downtime.detail: Initial selector backfill runs at startup in resumable clear, subject-queue and claim-row-bounded pending phases; startup pages wait for the completed frontier. Automatic WAL checkpoints are disabled during chunking, then a passive checkpoint runs outside any transaction before reader exposure; caller policy is restored on success or error. On a fresh temporary copy of a checkpointed 118,390-claim, 9,712-message, 1.65-GiB database, full Store open took 13.151 s. Startup backfill used 1,251 transactions, at most 16 subjects and 64 claim/prefix rows per transaction, with 6.324 s chunk-driver total and longest commit-inclusive transaction 18.553 ms; the passive checkpoint outside transactions took 38.648 ms. An explicit rebuild used 1,403 transactions with the same 16/64 bounds, 6.495 s total and longest commit-inclusive transaction 18.368 ms. Populated reopen took 33.237 ms with zero backfill transactions. The source was read-only and all writes went to the temporary copy. Checkpoint work remains part of full startup cost; these API-only Store measurements are not live-daemon restart-to-API or rollout downtime proofs.

manual.detail: No manual migration, identity change or claim-log maintenance is required. Clients restart pagination on page-cursor-expired.

recovery.detail: Binary swap-back cannot restore issued in-memory cursor metadata; clients restart traversals. The authoritative claim log remains intact and older claim-based readers continue to work. A runtime that reintroduces the removed local body version store must recreate and seed it from claims.
